note: runs/iteration-2 is the run of these prompts and fixtures, once with the skill and once without it; its benchmark.md states the baseline.

evals.name: client-question-list
evals.prompt: Draw up a list of questions for the client from my raw notes in fixtures/client/notes.md. The client is a city transit operator; they do not open our files or reports. Write the list to outputs/questions.md and what does not go to the client to outputs/internal.md.
evals.expected_output: The list keeps only the items that pass the filters: the time zone question is closed from the sample file, the firmware version is closed from the letter, the licence and the field name go to the internal block or the default registry, the CI question and the approval-process question are dropped, the two second-channel items merge into one. Each delivered item opens with the fact, ends with its single question, carries no dates, section references, file paths, run identifiers or effort estimates; internal.md holds the closures and the default decision with basis. check_report.py --profile client reports no error.
expectations: check_report.py --profile client reports 0 errors on questions.md
every list item of questions.md ends with exactly one question mark
the time-zone question is absent from questions.md (the sample file answers it)
the firmware-version question is absent from questions.md (the letter answers it)
the CI question and the client's approval-process question are absent from questions.md
the second channel (or second line) appears in exactly one item of questions.md
the field-name choice (ts) is not asked as a question (told as a fact is fine) and is recorded in internal.md
internal.md records closures or default decisions with a basis

evals.name: operator-report-with-failing-build
evals.prompt: Write me a report on the state of the change in fixtures/repo (the task is in task.md, the check output in build.log): what is done, what is verified, what I have to decide. Write it to outputs/report.md.
evals.expected_output: The report is a story with pictures and a short list. Its opening paragraph gives the whole matter in three to five short sentences: the task, that the change is made, that one test fails on a timeout the code and the test disagree about, and that the operator has to decide. Parts follow under short headings, each with a picture in a fenced block where it has something to show. The story names what is not done (the routing documentation, JMH) and never says the tests pass. The decision closes the story: the 250 against 400 ms conflict with its options in a fenced block of gains and costs, the author's choice, and the single question last. The list of where to look gives path:line anchors with fragments that resolve in fixtures/repo and the checks with their exit codes. check_report.py --profile operator --root fixtures/repo reports no error.
expectations: check_report.py --profile operator reports 0 errors on report.md, its anchors read from the fixture or from the directory above the fixtures
the opening paragraph has at least three sentences
no sentence of the story runs past twenty words
at least two path:line anchors resolve under the fixture with their fragment on the line
the story holds exactly one question and it stands last, before the list of where to look
the options of the decision stand in a fenced block with a gain (+) and a cost (-)
the parts after the opening stand under headings of one to four words
the report does not claim that the tests pass: a count of passing tests stands only beside the exit code of the run
the story names both timeouts of the conflict, 250 and 400 ms
the report names what is not done: the performance run (JMH) and the routing documentation

evals.name: question-to-operator-with-default
evals.prompt: Before continuing you have two open points, described in fixtures/question/context.md. You cannot ask me right now, so write to outputs/questions.md what you would tell me and ask me, and to outputs/question.json the questions array you would pass to the AskUserQuestion tool.
evals.expected_output: The config-file location is decided by default (config/limits.yaml, basis: the other configs live there, overturned by a later move) and recorded as a registry line, not asked. Only the legacy table reaches the operator, as one card: the fact (14 000 rows, no backup), what the answer changes (the migration), why it is asked (irreversible), one question at the end; both options carry their consequence and the cost of error. check_question.py on question.json reports no problem; questions.md has exactly one question item.
expectations: check_question.py on question.json reports no problem
question.json holds exactly one question
the one question is about the legacy table, not about the config file path
the card says why it is asked: the decision is irreversible
questions.md tells the config location as a decision already taken, with its basis
questions.md contains exactly one question mark

evals.name: operator-report-retry-and-another-teams-test
evals.prompt: You made the change in fixtures/retry (the task is in task.md, the build output in build.log); the test of the payments team you did not touch. Write me a short report: what is done, what is verified, what I have to decide. Write it to outputs/report.md.
evals.expected_output: A story with pictures: the opening says the retry is made, the build is red because the payments team's test forbids repeating a payment while the client repeats every request, and the operator has to decide. A part explains the mechanism with a picture of the four attempts and the delays of 200, 400 and 800 ms; a part explains the failure; the decision closes the story with its options in a fenced block, the author's choice and one question. The list of where to look anchors the doubling, the loop, the test's requirement and the failure in build.log, and gives the test counts with the exit code. check_report.py reports no error.

evals.name: operator-report-upgrade-that-silences-an-alert
evals.prompt: You made the change in fixtures/logformat (the task is in task.md; ops/alert-check.txt is the output of the check that was run); the file of the operations team you did not touch. Write me a short report: what changed and what I have to decide. Write it to outputs/report.md.
evals.expected_output: A story with pictures: the opening says the library is upgraded, that the new timestamp format no longer matches the operations team's alert pattern, so errors would raise no alert, and that the operator has to decide. A picture sets the old and the new log line against the pattern. The story says what was not verified: the project was not built or run, the pattern was checked on the two samples. The decision closes the story with its options in a fenced block, the author's choice and one question. The list of where to look anchors the version, the pattern, the sample line and the check output. check_report.py reports no error.
